## Why this unit matters

Define Product, User and Order boundaries. Keep API contracts small and explicit, then make the first Product HTTP call from Order.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Shop Service Decomposition](service-decomposition.qmd)**
2. **[Initial HTTP Service Calls](resttemplate-calls.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Checkout depends on both Product and User lookup results.

$$
\operatorname{Checkout}(p,u)=\operatorname{ValidateProduct}(p)\land\operatorname{ValidateUser}(u)
$$

This is a simplified precondition, not the complete transaction rule; persistence, inventory, security and payment constraints may add predicates.
